_readme: DJ's word on where peoples moved, for Through time (scripts/build_years_commoners.py migration_layers). Each keyframe is a year and the land of one or more of DJ's 1765 countries (data/canon/country-shapes.json), speaking one language (its id in data/languages.json) or "as in 1765" (what DJ's last commoners map shows there, as its stage in that year). Each is taken as one of his regional keyframes: between two of them the yearly map switches by the usual rule, outwards from the language's speakers. "where" limits a keyframe to part of its land, the rest speaking what this file had there before: "stateless" (the land no state held on the rulers' map that year) "east" / "west" / "north" / "south" (the islands or land farthest that way, a tenth of it), or {"near": a 1765 country, "km": distance} (the land that close to it). Add, change or delete entries freely, then rebuild (python scripts/build-years.py languages).

keyframes.note: Ashain's first people: the Mikrolean speakers, who left Quia soon after their split from Proto-Ankusano-Elaian (DJ, 19 Oct 2026)
still theirs when the Kingdom of Mara's colonists came; they moved on into Mahea

the ancestors of Ashain's people today came through and took over the islands (DJ, 19 Oct 2026): the Kingdom of Mara, from the east, in the 1st to 3rd centuries (wiki: Ashain; DJ chose the wiki's dates)
the islands slowly colonised by the 3rd century (wiki: Ashain)
Pelugrotoa before the Pelugrotoans came: Kiesian in the south, Tyrnotean along the Inania border (DJ, 19 Oct 2026)
